text.title: Continuous Discovery Examples
text.summary: End-to-end worked example illustrating the methodology against a realistic input.

example.title: Onboarding-friction discovery cycle
example.note: Daily Haiku watchers flag step-3 funnel drop 38% (posthog) + 12 Intercom tickets clustered as 'I do not understand step 3' over a week. Two interviews (paid + free) confirm: user expects automation, sees a blank textbox. Synthesizer (Sonnet) tags JTBD + user-segment + frequency + severity. Bi-weekly Opus run aggregates 5 observations across 4 sources (>=5 / >=2 floor passes). Creates opportunity opp_step3_friction with score (freq=12, sev=4, addr=H). Assumption-tester designs a fake-door variant + smoke test; ships test; assumption 'users want a 1-click template' returns 'evidence found' (47% click). Monthly review writes a memo: doubled-down on opp_step3_friction; kill list includes opp_old_chart_redesign (no evidence in 6 weeks).

example.title: Canonical cadence agent prompt
example.note: Standard cadence agent prompt with Torres rules:
example.code:
<role>You are the {agent}. Continuous Discovery (Torres) practitioner.</role>
<inputs> <since>{ISO8601 last-run timestamp}</since> <signals>{paths to analytics/tickets/transcripts}</signals> <ost>{path to opportunity-solution-tree.md}</ost> <assumptions>{path to open-assumptions.md}</assumptions> </inputs>
<rules> - Tag every observation with: source, user_segment, frequency, severity (1-5). - Distinguish OPPORTUNITY (unmet need) from SOLUTION (proposed feature). Reject solution-shaped input. - Never declare "validated" from a single signal. Require N>=5 across >=2 sources. - Surface curse-of-knowledge risk: flag claims that assume internal jargon. - Output JSON matching schema {schema_path}, plus a markdown digest <= 60 lines. </rules>
<task>{cadence-specific instruction}</task>
example.note: This is the structure required by rule canonical-prompt-structure; the rules block hardcodes ban-validated-word, n5-across-2-sources, opportunity-vs-solution-intake and curse-of-knowledge-lint.
